Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Sarah Smith, DOB: 20/04/1980 (clinician also stated 1983 – conflict noted), Gender: Female, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Not recorded (consultation conducted by Dr Gohil, Babylon tele-health). Practice: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded. Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Health-related anxiety/panic symptoms in the postpartum period (supported by patient report of feeling “really stressed,” palpitations, and DDx ranking “Anxiety/panic attack” – medium likelihood)
- Secondary: Acute shortness of breath – medical differential includes pulmonary embolism (high likelihood in DDx) → referred to emergency care (primary physical problem, but contributes to anxiety)
- Tertiary: Not recorded

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Codeine (post-operative analgesia; dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Allergies/ADRs: Ibuprofen – reaction not specified
- Past Medical History: Caesarean section 4 weeks ago; no other chronic illnesses reported

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Not recorded
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): Not recorded
- Family History: Mother with history of leg clots (DVT); no psychiatric conditions mentioned

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: At home with 4-week-old baby; partner at work at time of consult
- Social Support: Partner (working), mother (mentioned), no further detail
- Occupation/Education: Not recorded
- Alcohol Use: Not recorded
- Smoking/Substance Use: Not recorded
- Key Stressors: Recent surgery and caring for newborn; acute health concern (possible PE)

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Appears able to engage via video/phone; caring for infant; cooperative
- Mood & Affect: Reports feeling “really stressed”; affect congruent with anxiety
- Speech & Thought: Normal rate and flow; coherent; no thought disorder evident
- Perception: No hallucinations or perceptual disturbances reported

Cognition:
- Orientation: Oriented to person, place, time (able to give DOB, follow instructions)
- Attention/Concentration: Adequate (followed pulse-counting task)
- Memory: Not formally tested; no concerns raised
- Insight & Judgement: Insight into need for urgent medical review; judgement intact (agreed to present to hospital)

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Not recorded
- Appetite: Not recorded
- Motivation/Energy: Not recorded
- Anxiety Symptoms: Palpitations, subjective stress, shortness of breath (may be both medical and anxiety-related)

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Denied/not expressed
- Protective Factors: Caring for newborn; insight; willingness to seek help
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low (for self-harm); medical risk high → referred to ED
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
Predisposing: Postpartum physiological changes; limited sleep likely though not documented  
Precipitating: Sudden onset shortness of breath with potential serious medical cause  
Perpetuating: Health anxiety heightened by family history of clots and recent surgery  
Protective: Good insight; ability to follow medical advice; presence of partner/family support

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Postpartum health-related anxiety
- Patient Goal(s): “Feel less stressed and worried about my health” (goal inferred from stated stress; no explicit goal verbalised – not recorded)
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce acute anxiety, provide psycho-education on health anxiety and postpartum emotional health, arrange follow-up after medical clearance
- Actions (Patient): Attend ED for physical assessment; engage in relaxation/breathing strategies provided; schedule follow-up once medically stable
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide reassurance and brief grounding techniques; supply written information on postpartum mood/anxiety; organise review appointment after hospital visit; consider referral for psychological therapy (e.g., CBT) if anxiety persists

Secondary Problem: Acute SOB/possible pulmonary embolism (medical)
- Patient Goal(s): Obtain urgent assessment and treatment
- Clinical Goal(s): Rule out / treat PE; minimise medical drivers of anxiety
- Actions (Patient): Present to ED promptly, take baby supplies, withhold further codeine until reviewed
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Advised ED attendance; offered ambulance; documented plan to withhold opioids; communicated risk factors

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Need for urgent medical review; brief explanation of clots and PE; reassurance that hospital can rapidly treat; advised on not taking codeine pending review
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Return of sudden SOB, chest pain, severe anxiety/panic, palpitations
- Coping Strategies: Slow breathing exercise demonstrated (pulse-counting); seek partner/family support; present to ED if symptoms worsen

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Obtained verbally during consult
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Within 1–2 weeks post-hospital assessment or sooner if anxiety escalates

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
1. Anxiety/Panic Attack (Medium likelihood) – sudden stress, palpitations, dyspnea without objective exam findings; postpartum period increases risk  
2. Postpartum Pulmonary Embolism (High likelihood) – recent C-section, acute SOB, tachycardia, family history of DVT  
3. Acute Respiratory Infection (Medium likelihood) – new cough and pleuritic discomfort but no fever

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: formal psychiatric history, substance use details, comprehensive MSE, validated anxiety scale, specific treatment goals, follow-up arrangements in writing  
● Internal conflicts: DOB given as 20/04/1980; clinician restated 1983 (conflict noted)  
● Transcript quality notes: Mental health content limited; consultation focused on acute medical issue; no explicit discussion of mood/anxiety treatment goals or consent documentation
